items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: you were with Les Hites’s band... I was awed by him... They were very encouraging... filling his shoes at the time

ctx.x: Because I’ve not been there – it had an old dome, and this was the inscription on it. 19 years old, and I remember that to this day.

What was it like to join – you played in a number of bands, but here you were with Les Hites’s band, and you were on the road. Was it frightening to you to think, all right, this is a lot of pressure?

I was awed by him, because this was a band that was pretty well known. I just felt that I wasn’t adequate at that time. They were very encouraging. They had had another fellow playing first trumpet with them, [?Geidner] Campell, who was very fine. He was sick, I think. That was why he was leaving. It was difficult, filling his shoes at the time, because I didn’t have that kind of experience as a lead player. I hadn’t been the lead player in the bands I had played, except small groups.
